title: Bridge Matching Sampler: Scalable Sampling via Generalized Fixed-Point Diffusion Matching
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: Iterating simulate, resample, bridge-sample and regress steps transports a simple prior to the target with one stable objective.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right time axis, numbered step badges annotating trajectories
description: One wide panel shows a time axis running from t=0 at left to t=T at right. A blue Gaussian prior density, p_prior, sits on the left. A red bimodal target density, p_target, sits on the right, with a dashed grey density marking the current endpoint distribution. Grey noisy sample paths run between them, with one path in dark grey. A dashed purple Brownian-bridge path starts at a purple resampled point X0' and passes through a marked intermediate point X_t. Four yellow numbered circles label the steps. Step 1 is the SDE simulation formula, step 2 is resampling X0', step 3 is sampling X_t from the bridge, and step 4 is computing u_{i+1}. A grey 'Repeat steps 1 to 4' box at top left shows the loop. The eye goes first to the purple path and the numbered badges.
caption: Bridge Matching Sampler (BMS). Illustration of one outer iteration of our fixed-point algorithm. Starting from the current drift $u_i$, we (1) simulate the controlled forward SDE, $\dd X_t = \sigma(t)\,u_i(X_t,t)\,\dd t + \sigma(t)\,\dd B_t$, starting from $p_{\mathrm{prior}}$, to obtain $K$ trajectories with endpoints $(X_0,X_T)$ (grey curves); (2) resample the prior endpoints, replacing $X_0$ by an independent sample $X_0'\sim p_{\mathrm{prior}}$ to form the coupling $\Pi^i_{0,T}=p_{\mathrm{prior}}\otimes\P^{u_i}_T$; (3) sample intermediate states $X_t\sim\P_{t\mid 0,T}(\cdot\mid X_0', X_T)$ from the associated Brownian bridge (dashed purple); and (4) update the drift to $u_{i+1}$ by regressing it on the path-dependent target $\xi(X,t)$ via the matching objective described in [ref]. Iterating steps 1-4 drives the time marginals of the learned process towards $p_{\mathrm{target}}$ while maintaining a single, scalable, and stable training objective.
abstract: Sampling from unnormalized densities using diffusion models has emerged as a powerful paradigm. However, while recent approaches that use least-squares `matching' objectives have improved scalability, they often necessitate significant trade-offs, such as restricting prior distributions or relying on unstable optimization schemes. By generalizing these methods as special forms of fixed-point iterations rooted in Nelson's relation, we develop a new method that addresses these limitations, called Bridge Matching Sampler (BMS). Our approach enables learning a stochastic transport map between arbitrary prior and target distributions with a single, scalable, and stable objective. Furthermore, we introduce a damped variant of this iteration that incorporates a regularization term to mitigate mode collapse and further stabilize training. Empirically, we demonstrate that our method enables sampling at unprecedented scales while preserving mode diversity, achieving state-of-the-art results on complex synthetic densities and high-dimensional molecular benchmarks.
